## Summary of Modifications

### 1. **Modifications in each file**

- **`drivers/i3c/master/mipi-i3c-hci/dma.c`**  
  Added a mutex guard (`guard(mutex)(&hci->control_mutex)`) at the beginning of `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` to serialize concurrent calls to this function.

- **`drivers/i3c/master/mipi-i3c-hci/core.c`**  
  Added `mutex_init(&hci->control_mutex)` inside the probe function (`i3c_hci_probe`) to initialize the new mutex.

- **`drivers/i3c/master/mipi-i3c-hci/hci.h`**  
  Added a new member `struct mutex control_mutex` to the `struct i3c_hci` data structure.

### 2. **Relationships between the modifications**

The changes are all part of a single fix: introducing a mutex to protect `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` from race conditions.  
- The mutex is **defined** in the core data structure (`hci.h`).  
- It is **initialized** during device probe (`core.c`).  
- It is **acquired** and **released** in the critical section of `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` (`dma.c`), ensuring that only one instance of the function runs at a time when multiple transfers timeout simultaneously.  

This serialization prevents interference between parallel invocations (e.g., multiple threads stopping/restarting the DMA ring at unexpected times), thereby fixing the race condition.
